defects: Hypothesis compares n to the truncated value toNat c₁ (i.e. n ≤ toNat c₁ in ℕ) instead of comparing n directly to the cardinal c₁ itself (n ≤ c₁ in Cardinal order) as in the gold statement

This changes the mathematical content: for an infinite cardinal c, n ≤ c holds for every n : ℕ (gold), but n ≤ toNat c is false for all n ≥ 1 since toNat of an infinite cardinal is 0 — the two hypotheses are not equivalent

Because the produced hypothesis is stated purely in terms of ℕ order on the truncations, it renders the theorem essentially trivial (a ↔ b comparison over ℕ trivially forces a = b by taking n = a and n = b), losing the substantive cardinal-arithmetic content of the original theorem
Drops the gold's universe polymorphism between c and d (Cardinal.{u} vs Cardinal.{v}), requiring both cardinals to be in the same universe
